_comment: All tunable Loop Protection thresholds in ONE place (spec Section 3). The watchdog READS these; it never rewrites them (a threshold change rides the repo + rollout, like all Loop Protection data). Every ceiling here is also a SAFETY CAP under Skill 60 Signal S4: a raise without an operator stamp is itself a P1 (spec 5.1/5.2).

tick._locked: T5/Section 3: every 15 minutes, jittered. Zero model calls; cadence costs CPU only. The system that hunts furnaces must be structurally incapable of being one.

burn_in._locked: T5: DRY_RUN observe-only for the first 7 days on any box; then Tier 1 arms. armed=false is the ledger default until the operator runs `arm`.

d1_restart_velocity._source: Box A ~56,050 restarts; Box F 4,528-in-10h. pm2 jlist restarts / launchctl runs / docker RestartCount, delta per unit per tick. NEVER an env dump (name/status/pid/restarts ONLY).

d2_token_burn_rate._source: Operator box ~11,800 calls/week; Box C ~10-12M input tokens/day idle. Paid vs local split, correlated with initiated-session presence (Skill 60 S5 method).

d3_identical_signature._source: Generalized loop-detector.sh progress test, made content-based: rolling hash over (outcome class + tool-call name sequence + target) in the new-bytes-since-last-tick slice. Outcome 'OK' (a SUCCESSFUL turn) counts too, at the higher p1_repeat_success ceiling - the 2026-07-13 correction-wave loop was 'successful' turns end to end, invisible to failure-only hashing; per-contact batch sends never false-positive because the target differs per contact. Failures keep 3/5.

d4_timer_refire._source: Cron fires > 2x declared cadence = P1; healthy-probe-but-no-progress 3 ticks = P1 wedge; any orphan listener on :18789 = P1 (Box E deferral deadlock).

d5_transcript_poison._source: Derived from ONE archived operator-box incident transcript (4,607,807 bytes / 3,506 lines / 3,393 message records / 1,135 runtime tool-loop blocks) measured against a 70-file same-box healthy corpus. NOT round numbers: p1_blocks_per_burst=8 is the SMALLEST burst observed in that incident (bursts, gap<=3: 275,171,156,143,122,122,76,50,11,8,1), so firing at 8 catches 11/11 historical bursts while landing ~6.5% into the median burst - seconds to ~1 minute in, far before the ten-minute lane occupancy the incident cost. warn=3 sits one below the runtime's own identical-call guard. The ratio is a TRAILING window, never cumulative: the measured cumulative share was still only 0.122 at record 1250 while the local rate was already 0.244, so a whole-file ratio detector stays silent for thousands of records (a flow detector's false all-clear). Measured max trailing-200 share: poisoned 0.50, healthy corpus 0.0000 - warn 0.20 / P1 0.40 sit inside that gap. p1_poisoned_checkpoints=1 because a compaction summary that captured loop text verbatim is RE-INJECTED on resume and SURVIVES a session roll (measured: 7 of 16 checkpoint summaries poisoned, 163 block-signature hits) - the control archive carried 14 checkpoints and 0 hits, so 1 is safe. rearm_risk_bytes=2097152 is the OpenClaw memoryFlush forceFlushTranscriptBytes default (2 MiB), past which every compaction re-arms a forced flush; it is a SEVERITY MODIFIER ONLY and never fires alone - the control archive is 17,160,766 bytes (8x over it) with zero blocks and MUST stay silent. tail_bytes=2000000 matches the existing D3 slice bound and covered all 7 poisoned checkpoints (deepest at 1,617,348 bytes from end).

d6_futile_retry_burst._source: SEMANTIC repetition - the blind spot D3 and every runtime guard share, because they all key on the ARGUMENTS. Incident: an agent hit a fail-closed API and made 13 tool calls in 49s, every one a reworded attempt at the same intent; all 13 carried distinct arguments so the runtime's (toolName,argsHash) guard and this repo's stricter (toolName,argsHash,resultHash) runaway patch both stayed silent. NOT round numbers, and NOT count-only: measured against the operator box's REAL local corpus (998 transcripts, 388 with tool results, 12,465 toolResult records). That corpus contains a perfectly HEALTHY burst of 460 exec calls in 48.2s with 2 errors, plus ~100 file/tool pairs at >=13 calls per 60s - so a count-only detector keyed on the incident's own 13/49s would fire on roughly a quarter of all healthy sessions and is REJECTED as unshippable. Futility, never volume, is the signal. window_seconds=60 covers the incident's 49s span. FAILING-BURST face: at >=5 calls AND >=60% tool-layer errors the real corpus yields only 6 file/tool pairs (1.5% of files with tool results), and the P1 pair (>=10 calls AND >=90% errors) isolates a single measured 36-call/36-error read burst - a genuine loop. FAIL-CLOSED face, the primary one: auth-class refusals counted from the RESULT payload, because the incident's exec calls exited 0 and were recorded status=completed - the tool layer saw nothing wrong, which is exactly why every args-keyed and every error-keyed guard missed it. Measured on the same corpus with the strict marker set: only 13 file/tool pairs reach 3 auth-class results in a 60s window and the maximum observed is 6, so warn=3 (the first attempt past the doctrine's <=2) and p1=5 sit inside real headroom. doctrine_max_attempts=2 is the doctrine rule's own number, so the detector and the written rule cannot drift apart.

backoff._locked: Section 5.2/5.4: exponential backoff with jitter is the ONLY sanctioned retry shape. Base 2h (the never-stop doctrine's own number), doubling, capped 24h, state persisted on disk per job (a backoff that lives in memory resets to zero on the next crash).

escalation._locked: Section 7: an unacknowledged P1 goes to Rescue Rangers after 30 minutes; a dead-man P1 escalates immediately. Thresholds shared with Skill 60.
